subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Neurocutaneous Syndromes: TSC, NF-1, and Sturge-Weber

steps.tx: Autosomal dominant mutations in the TSC1 or TSC2 genes disrupt normal inhibition of the mTOR intracellular signaling cascade. Arising from defects in hamartin or tuberin, **tuberous sclerosis complex** (TSC) produces widespread benign hamartomatous growths across the brain, skin, eyes, kidneys, and heart. The classic clinical triad of Vogt consists of facial adenoma sebaceum, refractory seizures, and intellectual disability, although only one-third exhibit all three.
steps.say: Tuberous sclerosis is an autosomal dominant hamartomatous disorder caused by TSC1 or TSC2 mutations. Vogt triad comprises facial angiofibromas, seizures, and intellectual disability.

vis.alt: Clinical and neuroimaging collage displaying facial angiofibromas, ash-leaf macules, and subependymal calcified tubers.
vis.caption: Cutaneous and cerebral hamartomatous lesions characteristic of tuberous sclerosis complex. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Cutaneous manifestations frequently provide the earliest diagnostic clinical markers in young infants presenting with seizures. Examination with a Wood lamp reveals pathognomonic **ash-leaf hypomelanotic macules in TSC**, defined as three or more polygonal or lance-ovate amelanotic macules visible at birth. Later cutaneous markers include facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum) appearing over the malar bridge at school age, shagreen patches over the lumbosacral region, and periungual Koenen fibromas.
steps.say: Ash-leaf hypopigmented macules visible under Wood lamp are the earliest sign of tuberous sclerosis in infants. Malar facial angiofibromas develop later in childhood.

rows: Present at birth or early infancy
Major criterion; enhanced under Wood lamp
Reddish-brown papules over nose and cheeks
Emerges at 4 to 8 years of age
Fleshy nodules beneath or beside nails

steps.tx: Hamartomatous cellular disorganization within the cerebral mantle drives early-life refractory epilepsy. Cortical tubers and calcified subependymal nodules line the lateral ventricles, giving a candle-dripping appearance. In five to fifteen percent of patients, benign **subependymal giant cell astrocytoma** (SEGA) arises near the foramen of Monro, threatening acute obstructive hydrocephalus. Oral mTOR inhibitors like everolimus induce significant regression of SEGAs and renal angiomyolipomas.
steps.say: Subependymal nodules resemble candle guttering along the ventricles, while subependymal giant cell astrocytomas can obstruct the foramen of Monro. Oral everolimus shrinks these tumors.

left.title: CNS Hamartomatous Lesions
points: Cortical tubers: glioneuronal disorganization in cortex
Subependymal nodules: calcified nodules lining ventricles
High association with infantile spasms in infancy

steps.tx: Autosomal dominant mutations in the NF1 gene on chromosome 17q11.2 cause the most common neurocutaneous disorder. Arising from loss of the tumor suppressor protein neurofibromin, **neurofibromatosis type 1** (Recklinghausen disease) demonstrates complete penetrance with variable expressivity. The disorder is characterized by neural crest-derived peripheral nerve sheath tumors, distinctive pigmentary skin lesions, skeletal dysplasias, and optic pathway gliomas.
steps.say: Neurofibromatosis type one is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by NF1 mutations on chromosome 17. It features cafe-au-lait macules, neurofibromas, and optic gliomas.

rows: Present in infancy; increases with age
Crowe sign: clustered small freckles in skin folds

steps.tx: Characteristic ophthalmological and osseous lesions complete the established clinical diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy identifies benign **Lisch nodules of the iris**, representing pigmented melanocytic iris hamartomas present in over ninety percent of affected adults. Classic skeletal abnormalities include sphenoid wing dysplasia causing pulsating exophthalmos, congenital anterolateral tibial pseudarthrosis, and optic pathway gliomas.
steps.say: Lisch nodules are asymptomatic iris hamartomas visible on slit-lamp exam. Skeletal hallmarks include sphenoid wing dysplasia and tibial pseudarthrosis.

left.title: Ophthalmological Criteria
points: Lisch nodules (>=2 iris hamartomas on slit lamp)
Optic pathway glioma (presents in young children)
Visual field testing and annual MRI surveillance
Proptosis or precocious puberty if chiasm involved

right.title: Distinctive Skeletal Lesions
points: Sphenoid wing dysplasia causing pulsatile proptosis
Congenital bowing and pseudarthrosis of tibia

steps.tx: Bilateral vestibular schwannomas distinguish neurofibromatosis type 2 as a separate clinical and genetic entity. Caused by mutations in the NF2 tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 22q12 encoding merlin (schwannomin), **neurofibromatosis type 2** is characterized by bilateral eighth cranial nerve vestibular schwannomas, multiple intracranial meningiomas, spinal ependymomas, and posterior subcapsular juvenile cataracts, while cutaneous cafe-au-lait spots are sparse.
steps.say: Neurofibromatosis type two arises from NF2 mutations on chromosome 22, presenting with bilateral acoustic neuromas, meningiomas, and juvenile cataracts.

steps.tx: Congenital persistence of embryological cephalic vascular plexus produces unilateral capillary facial and leptomeningeal angiomatosis. Characterized by somatic mosaic activating mutations in the GNAQ gene, **Sturge-Weber syndrome** (encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis) features a facial port-wine stain (nevus flammeus) in the distribution of the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma, intractable focal seizures, intellectual disability, and congenital glaucoma.
steps.say: Sturge-Weber syndrome is a sporadic disorder caused by GNAQ mutations. It features a facial port-wine stain over the ophthalmic nerve, leptomeningeal angiomatosis, and glaucoma.

rows: Tram-track gyral cortical calcification on skull X-ray

steps.tx: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion beneath the leptomeningeal angioma triggers progressive gyral atrophy and calcification. Skull radiography and computed tomography demonstrate pathognomonic **tram-track cortical calcification**, consisting of parallel gyriform calcifications along the atrophic cerebral cortex underlying the angioma. Intractable infantile focal seizures provoke progressive hemiparesis, hemianopia, and cognitive regression, often requiring surgical hemispherotomy.
steps.say: Tram-track gyriform cortical calcification under the leptomeningeal angioma is the radiological hallmark. Intractable seizures may require hemispherectomy.

left.title: Radiological Hallmarks on CT / MRI
points: Enlarged ipsilateral choroid plexus with hypervascularity
Lack of normal cortical superficial venous drainage

right.title: Comprehensive Management Goals
points: Aggressive anticonvulsant control of focal seizures
Low-dose aspirin to prevent microvascular thrombosis
Early functional hemispherotomy for refractory epilepsy
